text:
Owen Tippett scored 28 goals for Philadelphia last season. Seventeen games into this one, he has 2, his ice time has slipped below 15 minutes a night, and a trade-rumor site has linked him to Seattle. That is a lot of noise around a winger whose tools haven't changed: NHL Edge has his top skating speed in the 98th percentile and his hardest shot in the 97th.

Most of the slump is finishing. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, are 3.46, and he is scoring on 5.4% of his shots, far below the range our numbers expect for him. Teammates have also scored 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and that usually swings back. The worry is real, though: his chance rate is down from last season, and at five-on-five the Flyers have had only about 41% of the chance quality with him out there, worse than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains what he looks like at his best: 60% of his shots came off the rush, and he carries the puck in on 54% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey added that he draws more penalties than he takes.
headline: Owen Tippett's goals have dried up, and the rumors have started
